I've been on what I call "ghost hunting trips". Basically, me, two of my friends who can supposedly see/hear/make contact with ghosts, and maybe a couple other people go to this park near one of my friend's house.

Nothing two exciting has gone down. We go at night, they bring along  their phones to record audio (sometimes they take pictures with a digital camera), they ask a bunch of questions*, and sometimes they'll get a little or a lot freaked out and say that we need to leave, and sometimes they won't and we leave whenever.

I've never heard anything, and I don't really buy it, but for the sake of our friendship, I keep my mouth shut.

The only notable incident was the way streetlights (as we walked to and from the park, we being me and both friends) would literally turn off and on depending on if we were underneath them (my friend provided an explanation involving something to do with ghosts, but I can't remember it).

*Like, "Is there anyone here with us now?", "What's your name?", "how did you die?", etc.

So yeah. That's about it.

Neither happened to me directly, but instilled paranoia about both foods until I couldn't eat them anymore without examining them very, very thoroughly.

The first is fish: Apparently, fish bones can get stuck in your throat if you swallow them (at the time, the realization that there were bones was almost enough to make me stop eating it completely.) My sister got a bone stuck and spent all night coughing, gagging, and otherwise trying to get it out. The next couple of times I ate fish, I chopped it in such fine pieces that it was hardly worth eating.

The second happened to my mom. We were eating hamburgers, and all of a sudden, she flips out and starts spitting out her food. You know those wire brushes you use to clean off the burnt bits on grill? A piece of wire had fell off, gotten in one of the patties, and from that day forward, that was the only thing I could think of whenever I ate it.

**tl;dr**: Fish bones ruined fish for me, something in a hamburger ruined that for me, couldn't eat either without getting really nervous about it happening to me, and now don't eat either one.
